answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A meadow delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A orchard check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A nectar penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 7412 identities need 7412 bonds of 27 tokens, 42413 dollars of hardware and 15 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
